crossfade.note: For a two-<audio> player: when A reaches aFrom, start B at bAt (better: at A.currentTime - (cycles - 1) * cycleSeconds) and crossfade with equal-power curves over `seconds`. Both are drone only and at the same point of the tanpura cycle; anywhere inside quietInCycle works.

xfade.note: Samples [N, N+T) repeat [0, T). Crossfade two elements inside the tail: when A reaches loopSeconds + d, start B at d; both then play identical audio.

loop.note: The whole file is one seamless loop. Decoders that read the gapless header (Chromium decodeAudioData, ffmpeg) return exactly `samples` samples: loop the whole AudioBuffer (AudioBufferSourceNode.loop = true). A decoder that ignores the header returns more, usually 1105 extra at the start (576 encoder + 529 decoder delay): then set loopStart = 1105 / sampleRate and loopEnd = loopStart + samples / sampleRate. Avoid <audio loop>: Chromium 141 skips 12–23 ms at the wrap (measured), an audible hiccup in the drone. A player that crossfades two <audio> elements should use music.tanpura.crossfade (same point of the tanpura cycle) rather than fade the end of the file into B started at 0.
